What's so amazing about tigers?

The tiger, the largest of the cat family, is a splendid yet familiar animal that often appears in old Korean folk tales. And there's an amazing secret hidden in its stripes.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about tigers

A tiger's black stripes on an orange background work as camouflage that hides its body in the tall grass. Amazingly, the stripes are all different from one tiger to the next, just like fingerprints. With excellent night vision, soft padded paws, and retractable claws, it hunts without a sound. Unlike most of the cat family, it loves water and swims well, and it's a solitary animal that lives alone. In the wild, it's an endangered species.

Great points to observe together

Point out things like the stripes (camouflage and fingerprints), night vision, retractable claws, and swimming. It's great to talk together about, "Isn't it amazing that every tiger's stripes are different?"

Parent guide — how to grow curiosity

Compare the stripes in tiger photos and find out how "they're all different!" Compare the ways it resembles a cat (claws and whiskers), and use the story of its being endangered to nurture a caring heart for living things.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Are all tiger stripes the same?
A. No. Just like a person's fingerprints, they're all different from one tiger to the next. You can tell tigers apart by their stripes.

Q. Do tigers like water?
A. Yes. Unlike most of the cat family, they love water and swim well.

Q. How can we observe them at home?
A. Comparing stripes in photos, finding what resembles a cat, and the story of its being endangered all work well.
